verdict.rationale: No option clearly dominates on the stated facts. D is earliest at the hotel and has only one connection, favoring next-morning readiness, but is the most expensive. C is the cheapest and nearly as early, but requires two relatively short connections. B is inexpensive and has a nonstop flight, but substitutes a long evening drive for connection risk. A costs more than B and arrives only slightly earlier, but its long connection may be attractive to a traveler prioritizing missed-connection resilience and avoiding the MSY-to-Lafayette drive. Selecting among these tradeoffs requires an unstated preference or travel policy concerning cost, connection risk, driving, and arrival priority.
